$comment: See README.md in this directory for what these numbers are and are not.

provenance.summary: Generic, conservative baseline failure rates by media class and age band. These are NOT vendor-published figures and are NOT attributed to any fleet study.
provenance.why_generic: Per-model annualized failure rates vary by an order of magnitude between drive families, and a wrong number carrying a real citation is worse than an honest default. Published per-model data exists and can be loaded on top of this file; see per_model below.

recommended_source.name: Backblaze Drive Stats
recommended_source.note: Publishes quarterly annualized failure rates per model. Enter the figures for your own models under per_model; each entry records its own source and retrieval date.

base_afr.$comment: Annualized probability that a drive of this media class fails, before age, duty, SMART and bus adjustments.

age_factor.$comment: Bathtub curve. Year 0 is elevated (infant mortality), years 1-3 are the floor, and risk climbs from year 4. Bands are [min_years, max_years, multiplier]; the last band applies to anything older.

duty_factor.$comment: HDD duty is power-on hours; SSD duty is bytes written against the endurance rating. Bands are [min, max, multiplier].

smart_factor.$comment: A pending sector is a step change, not a nudge: the drive has data it cannot read and has not yet been able to relocate. Multipliers are applied together; see risk.py for the exact combination.

pending_sector.note: Dominates when non-zero. One is enough to change the answer.

crc_errors.note: Interface or cable errors rather than media errors. Real, but usually a bad cable or bridge rather than a dying platter.

unverified.note: Applied when a drive reports no error counters at all. A drive verified clean and a drive that said nothing are not in the same state: the second could have fifty pending sectors and no way to tell. Uncertainty is a cost, and pricing it at 1.0 would rank an unverifiable drive alongside one known to be healthy.

bus_factor.$comment: The enclosure and bridge are part of the failure unit: a USB bridge that dies takes access to the drive with it, and SMART is often unavailable through one.

correlation.$comment: Copies that fail together are not two copies. Applied to the joint loss probability of a set of drives.
correlation.note: batch_key is manufacturer + model + purchase month. Two drives from one purchase order share a manufacturing batch, a shelf, an environment and a duty cycle; their failures are correlated well above independence.

per_model.$comment: Populate from published fleet data. Each entry: {"afr": <float>, "source": "<name>", "url": "<url>", "retrieved_at": "<YYYY-MM-DD>"}. Matched on a normalised model string; takes precedence over base_afr.
